a: Layered architecture separates presentation, business, and data layers.
Hexagonal (ports/adapters) isolates domain logic from external interfaces.
Event-driven systems communicate by publishing and consuming events.
CQRS separates read models from write models for scalability and clarity.
Event sourcing stores state as a sequence of events instead of only latest row state.
A modular monolith is one deployable unit with strong internal module boundaries.
SOA organizes capabilities as interoperable services, often with an ESB historically.
Backend-for-Frontend provides an API tailored to a specific client (web/mobile).
A sidecar container adds supporting features (proxy, logging) beside the main app.
Ambassador proxies outbound traffic for retries, discovery, and monitoring.
An ACL translates between your domain model and an external legacy model.
Strangler fig incrementally replaces a legacy system by routing pieces to new services.
